notes: Product of both independent process claims. Merged from the claim 6 preamble (L150), the claim 13 preamble (L175) and compound claim 19 (L191), which claims the same genus per se. A Markush genus with variable R1 and R2, so it names no one compound and is left unresolved; formula II is a pointer to a drawing that this section never states a name for. The R1 and R2 definitions at L156, L158, L175 and L191 define substituents and are not emitted as compounds. The drawn formula II at L177 and L193 is a Markush generic and its IMAGE_EXTRACT carries no molecules, so no structure reached this record. Claim 20 (L195) narrows R1 to chlorine and R2 to (C2)alkyl but prints no name for the compound that results, so no record is created for it and its existence is recorded here instead.

Substrate of both independent process claims. Merged from claim 6 (L152) and claim 13 (L175). A Markush genus with variable R1 and R2, so it names no one compound and is left unresolved; formula I is a pointer to a drawing that this section never states a name for. The drawn formula I at L179 is a Markush generic and its IMAGE_EXTRACT carries no molecules, so no structure reached this record.

Brominating agent of claim 6, process variant A. Printed N-bromosuccimide at L154, a misprint; the identifier is the corrected spelling, which is one the document itself prints in the description, and the EN line at L155 reads it the same way. The as-printed variant is carried in aliases.

The co-reagent of the claim 6 process, charged alongside N-bromosuccinimide. A class term and not a named compound, so resolved is false and unresolved_reference is true. L154 prints it as a radical initiator and L160 as the radical initiator; per PROMPT-CORRECTIONS section 9 the identifier is the bare noun phrase with the article dropped and both as-printed forms go in aliases, so this record joins the same class term recorded in Background, Summary of the Invention and Process Conditions rather than splitting one class across several keys. Claim 7 (L160) enumerates the two members the class may take, azoisobutyronitrile and dibenzoyl peroxide, and those are kept as their own records: a class name identifies no single molecule, and claim 6 stands without claim 7, so recording only the members would leave the broader claim unrecorded. role is reagent and compound_class is reagent per PROMPT-CORRECTIONS section 8: an initiator is consumed in fragmenting to the chain-carrying radical and so does not meet A1 rule 9's definition of catalyst. commercially_available is false because nothing in this section states it.

One of the two radical initiators claim 7 (L160) allows for the variant A bromination. Printed correctly on this line, so no alias is carried. It is kept as a record separate from the class term radical initiator that claim 6 charges, which is recorded on its own. The closed role list has no initiator value; reagent is chosen because the list's catalyst is defined as not consumed and an initiator is consumed in fragmenting to the chain-carrying radical. That vocabulary gap is recorded rather than hidden.

The second radical initiator claim 7 (L160) allows for the variant A bromination. It is kept as a record separate from the class term radical initiator that claim 6 charges, which is recorded on its own. The closed role list has no initiator value; reagent is chosen because the list's catalyst is defined as not consumed and an initiator is consumed. The examples of this patent show the consumption directly, recharging this initiator through the reaction. That vocabulary gap is recorded rather than hidden.
Merged from claim 9 (L167), the solvent for variant A, and claim 15 (L183), the solvent for variant B. One record, not one per claim.
Alternative solvent for the variant A bromination, claim 10 (L169). Claim 12 (L173) then puts that bromination at the reflux temperature of this solvent.

Brominating agent of claim 13 (L175), process variant B, printed there as elemental bromine. That is the only occurrence of bromine in this section that names a substance; bromine at L156, L175 and L191 is a permitted value of the substituent R1 and is not emitted.

Alternative solvent for the variant B bromination, claim 16 (L185). Claim 18 (L189) then puts that bromination at the reflux temperature of this solvent. Kept as the name the patent prints rather than as dichloromethane.

The only fully enumerated compound name in the section. It appears solely as the compound excluded from the genus of compound claim 19 (L191), hence role other and is_section_product false. Printed there as 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-benzoic acid; that variant is carried in aliases and the identifier is a spelling the document prints elsewhere. commercially_available is false because Example 1 of this patent prepares it.
